argumentsAgainst: A VRRR auction is a short-term liquidity-management operation, not by itself evidence of a change in the policy repo rate or the monetary-policy stance.
The notified amount is an auction ceiling; the record does not establish the amount actually absorbed or the auction outcome.
argumentsFor: It provides the RBI with a flexible instrument to absorb surplus liquidity for a specified period.
Variable-rate bidding can help discover the market-clearing rate rather than impose a fixed absorption rate.
The overnight tenor limits the duration of the intervention and allows liquidity conditions to be reassessed quickly.

indiaImplications: The operation can help align overnight money-market liquidity with the RBI’s operating framework.
Temporary liquidity absorption may moderate excess funds available for deployment in short-term markets, although the record does not quantify the broader market effect.
Repeated use would require assessment alongside inflation, credit conditions and durable-liquidity trends; this notice alone does not establish those conditions.

officialFacts.text: The Reserve Bank of India decided to conduct a Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
The notified amount for the auction is ₹50,000 crore, with a tenor of one day.
The auction window is 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM.
The date of reversal is November 20, 2026 (Friday).
The operational guidelines for the auction given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2019-2020/1947 dated February 13, 2020 will remain the same.

sections.heading: Scheduled operation
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India announced an overnight VRRR auction under LAF for November 19, 2026. The notified amount was ₹50,000 crore, the tenor was one day, the window was 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM, and reversal was scheduled for November 20, 2026. [P1]

sections.heading: Mechanism and limit
paragraphs: A VRRR auction can temporarily draw funds from eligible participants to the RBI, with return after the stated tenor. Because the rate is variable and bids are auction-based, the operation is flexible. The notice confirms continuation of the February 13, 2020 operational guidelines but does not state the accepted bids or realised absorption. [P1]

use: Use the notice as a contemporary example of how the RBI can conduct time-bound, auction-based liquidity management under LAF; avoid treating the notified amount as realised absorption or the operation as a policy-rate decision.

advisory_notes: “Reverse repo operation” background should note that the RBI’s current framework also includes the SDF and that fixed-rate reverse repo use is discretionary.[3]
“Market-clearing rate” is a reasonable analytical characterization, but the supplied notice does not state the auction’s accepted-rate outcome.
“Temporary liquidity absorption may moderate excess funds” is analytical and should not be read as an observed market effect from this notice.
The claim that VRRR bids are placed by “eligible participants” and involve collateral is background supported by RBI’s framework, not by the notice itself.[3]
The conclusion that an overnight tenor permits rapid reassessment is sound analysis, but it is not an explicit finding in the notice.
The syllabus anchor is substantively relevant to monetary policy, liquidity management and LAF; GS3.2 is acceptable only if the taxonomy defines it as the relevant monetary-policy subsection.

“RBI schedules one-day VRRR auction to manage liquidity” is a headline-level inference; the notice says the decision followed a review of liquidity conditions but does not expressly state “to manage liquidity.”
The hypothetical is properly labelled, but “more funds than they wish to deploy overnight” is illustrative rather than a reported condition.

wayForward: Interpret VRRR announcements together with money-market rates, durable liquidity, credit conditions and inflation data.
Separate the notified amount, accepted amount and net liquidity impact when analysing an auction.
Maintain clear communication on the operational purpose and temporary tenor of liquidity interventions.
Use the referenced February 13, 2020 guidelines for procedural details rather than inferring them from this notice.
whyInNews: The Reserve Bank of India announced on November 18, 2026 that it would conduct an overnight VRRR auction under the LAF on November 19, 2026. The notified amount was ₹50,000 crore, with a one-day tenor, a 10:30 AM–11:00 AM window and reversal on November 20, 2026. [P1]
